title: Most Adults Cannot Pass This Social Worker Entrance Exam
summary: Explore Listening and Choice, Privacy and Perspective, Strengths and Boundaries, Safety and Records, Shared Decisions across five six-question rounds.

landing.intro:
Listen, understand and reflect.
Choose a thoughtful next step.

about.body:
Five rounds offer different angles on this challenge: Listening and Choice, Privacy and Perspective, Strengths and Boundaries, Safety and Records, Shared Decisions. Each round contains six distinct questions.

Choose one of four answers and move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. The target is 24 correct answers out of 30. The result describes this quiz attempt only.

For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited social-work admission, licensing or employment exam, and it is not professional or safeguarding advice. Laws, reporting duties and professional standards vary by location.

steps: Press Start, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question and progress through five rounds.
Complete all 30 questions to reveal your result. You can then unlock the full breakdown.

socialworker-q1.question: Which opening question is most likely to help a person explain what support they want?

answers.a1: What would you most like help with today?
answers.a2: Why did you let this happen?
answers.a3: Do you agree that my plan is best?
answers.a4: Can we skip the background and complete the form?

socialworker-q2.question: What is essential for informed consent?

answers.a1: A professional deciding what is best without discussion
answers.a2: The person understands the relevant information and agrees voluntarily
answers.a3: A signed form in every possible situation
answers.a4: Agreement from a family member instead of the person

socialworker-round1-new1.question: What does an open question encourage?

answers.a1: An account in the person's own words
answers.a2: Only a yes-or-no answer
answers.a3: Agreement with a hidden assumption
answers.a4: Silence about priorities

socialworker-round1-new2.question: Why summarise what a person has said and check it with them?

answers.a1: To confirm understanding
answers.a2: To replace their account with yours
answers.a3: To guarantee agreement
answers.a4: To end all further discussion

answers.a1: Planning with attention to the person's goals and preferences
answers.a2: Using one identical plan for everyone
answers.a3: Making every decision without the person
answers.a4: Ignoring available support

socialworker-round1-new4.question: Why explain your role at the start of contact?

answers.a1: To clarify what support and limits the person can expect
answers.a2: To promise every problem will be solved
answers.a3: To avoid discussing confidentiality
answers.a4: To remove the person's choices

socialworker-q3.question: Which statement about confidentiality is most accurate?

answers.a1: Information can never be shared for any reason
answers.a2: Everything may be shared with anyone on the support team
answers.a3: Privacy is protected, but serious safety concerns or legal duties may require limited sharing
answers.a4: Confidentiality ends after the first meeting

socialworker-q4.question: Which response best demonstrates cultural humility?

answers.a1: Assume everyone from the same background has similar needs
answers.a2: Avoid discussing culture under all circumstances
answers.a3: Use a standard plan before hearing the person's perspective
answers.a4: Ask about the person's preferences and remain open to correcting your assumptions

socialworker-round2-new1.question: What does a privacy notice or explanation help clarify?

answers.a1: How relevant information may be used and shared
answers.a2: A guarantee that nothing can ever be shared
answers.a3: Only the worker's office hours
answers.a4: The outcome of every assessment

socialworker-round2-new2.question: Which response avoids making an unsupported cultural assumption?

answers.a1: Ask what matters to the individual
answers.a2: Assume everyone from one background wants the same support
answers.a3: Use nationality to predict all preferences
answers.a4: Avoid asking any questions

socialworker-round2-new3.question: What is the purpose of professional supervision?

answers.a1: Reflection, accountability and support for practice
answers.a2: Replacing all personal responsibility
answers.a3: Sharing gossip without purpose
answers.a4: Guaranteeing no difficult decisions arise

socialworker-round2-new4.question: What should you do if you do not understand a person's communication needs?

answers.a1: Ask and arrange appropriate support
answers.a2: Assume they have nothing to say
answers.a3: Speak only to others about them
answers.a4: Proceed without checking understanding

socialworker-q5.question: What is a strengths-based assessment most likely to explore?

answers.a1: The person's abilities, resources, relationships and goals as well as their needs
answers.a2: Only the problems listed on a referral
answers.a3: Whether the person agrees with every professional opinion
answers.a4: Which service requires the least documentation

socialworker-q6.question: A person receiving support asks their social worker for a personal loan. What is the best general response?

answers.a1: Lend a small amount but keep it private
answers.a2: Maintain the professional boundary and explore appropriate sources of practical support
answers.a3: Ask another person receiving support to provide it
answers.a4: End all support immediately without explanation

socialworker-round3-new1.question: Which question looks for an existing strength?

answers.a1: What has helped you manage this before?
answers.a2: Why can you never cope?
answers.a3: Who is entirely to blame?
answers.a4: Why should we ignore your preferences?

answers.a1: People and services that can provide relevant help
answers.a2: Only a person's employer
answers.a3: Only government agencies
answers.a4: A list of every person met once

answers.a1: To keep the relationship safe and focused on its purpose
answers.a2: To prevent respectful communication
answers.a3: To deny every practical request
answers.a4: To eliminate all flexibility in support

socialworker-round3-new4.question: What makes a goal easier to review?

answers.a1: A clear description of the change sought and how it will be checked
answers.a2: Wording so vague nobody can assess it
answers.a3: No agreed time for review
answers.a4: A target chosen without discussion

socialworker-q7.question: A conversation raises a credible concern that a child or vulnerable adult may be unsafe. What is the best general next step?

answers.a1: Investigate every detail alone before telling anyone
answers.a2: Ignore it unless physical evidence is available
answers.a3: Record the concern and follow the applicable safeguarding or reporting process promptly
answers.a4: Post an anonymous account online for advice

socialworker-q8.question: Which case note is generally the most appropriate?

answers.a1: A delayed note based mainly on memory
answers.a2: A personal opinion about the person's character
answers.a3: Every detail from the worker's entire day
answers.a4: A timely, relevant and factual record that distinguishes observation from opinion

socialworker-round4-new1.question: What should a record say about an unverified concern?

answers.a1: Who reported it and what remains unconfirmed
answers.a2: That it is definitely true
answers.a3: Nothing because uncertainty exists
answers.a4: Only the worker's preferred explanation

socialworker-round4-new2.question: Why avoid promising absolute secrecy when harm may be involved?

answers.a1: Relevant safety or legal duties may require action
answers.a2: Because privacy never matters
answers.a3: Because every conversation must be public
answers.a4: Because the worker can share anything freely

socialworker-round4-new3.question: What is the purpose of a timely case note?

answers.a1: Supporting continuity and an accurate account of decisions
answers.a2: Replacing discussion with the person
answers.a3: Proving the plan cannot change
answers.a4: Recording unrelated personal opinions

socialworker-round4-new4.question: When risk appears to increase, what should happen?

answers.a1: Review the situation and follow the appropriate response process
answers.a2: Keep the old plan unchanged automatically
answers.a3: Wait for someone else to notice
answers.a4: Delete earlier records

socialworker-q9.question: When working with other professionals, which information-sharing approach is generally strongest?

answers.a1: Share relevant information lawfully, involve the person where possible and disclose no more than necessary
answers.a2: Send the full record automatically to every service
answers.a3: Never share information even when a serious safety duty applies
answers.a4: Rely only on informal verbal updates

socialworker-q10.question: A capable adult understands the options but declines a voluntary service. What is the best general response?

answers.a1: Pressure them until they agree
answers.a2: Check understanding and immediate safety, explain available options and respect the informed choice unless another legal duty applies
answers.a3: Contact their employer to persuade them
answers.a4: Remove every future route back to support

socialworker-round5-new1.question: What does advocacy aim to support?

answers.a1: A person's voice, rights and access to relevant help
answers.a2: A worker's personal preferences only
answers.a3: Guaranteed agreement with every request
answers.a4: Decisions made without listening

socialworker-round5-new2.question: Why review a support plan with the person?

answers.a1: Needs, preferences and circumstances can change
answers.a2: The first plan is always wrong
answers.a3: Reviewing removes all risks
answers.a4: The person's view matters only once

socialworker-round5-new3.question: A service is unavailable. What is a constructive response?

answers.a1: Explain honestly and explore suitable alternatives
answers.a2: Promise access you cannot provide
answers.a3: Blame the person
answers.a4: Record that support was provided anyway

socialworker-round5-new4.question: Which approach best handles a disagreement about a plan?

answers.a1: Explore the reasons, explain options and document the decision appropriately
answers.a2: Treat disagreement as automatic incapacity
answers.a3: Stop listening immediately
answers.a4: Hide the person's concerns
